recipes.name: Channa Masala (Chickpea Curry)
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
2 (15 ounce) cans garbanzo beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, about half the onion, the ginger, and rice flour in a blender; blend into a paste.

Heat the oil and cumin seeds in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the cumin swells and turns golden brown. Cook the remaining onion in the hot oil for about 3 minutes. Stir the blended tomato mixture, garbanzo beans, curry powder, and salt into the onions; cover and cook until hot, about 5 minutes. Garnish with the cilantro to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Channa Masala (Chickpea Curry)
raw_recipe.description: This fantastic Indian vegetarian curry recipe is great with Indian-style breads or rice.

review.reviewBody: really, really good and very easy to prepare. I used ground cumin instead, adding after cooking the onions 5 minutes, and also added 8 0z. of yogurt at the end, cooking maybe 5 minutes.

Things I did.. I marinated my garbanzo beans in some garam masala overnight. This adds depth to the dish. 
I sauteed the onion in canola oil, added ginger then (1) 28oz can of chopped tomatoes. Cooked thoroughly. Added beans and used an immersion blender to puree a little bit. I then added (1) 14oz can of lite coconut milk. Cooked a little further. Tasted it to check to see if it needed anything. I added a couple more shakes of garam masala. Simmered on the stove for another 10 minutes. Served over rice. Only giving it 3 stars b/c as written I think it needs some tweaking. Possibly 4 stars with my tweaking. Thanks for sharing !

I changed a lot of the recipe because of missing items and spontaneity. I tripled my recipe with the intention of eating leftovers. I used about 1/4 of a white onion, a small can of black olives, and about 1/3 cup of mushrooms. I also used garlic powder and completely omitted the ginger. I didn’t have coriander so I used parsley instead. I ended up using only one can of coconut milk even though tripling the recipe would mean three (one was enough). Lastly, I used cornstarch to thicken up my sauce at the end! It came out delicious and I would love to try using this recipe with chicken next time around. My boyfriend loved it.

This was really good! I prefer making my own chickpeas so I used my Instant Pot to cook the chickpeas. I also wanted to add some other vegetables so I added sweet potato. I’m sure it would have also been great without it. 
Since I added the extra sweet potato I knew I would need to add a little more seasoning, so I added Garam Masala as some had suggested.
We ate it with brown rice.

I made it as stated, except I cooked the onions until lightly caramelized. Also, I added a bit of garam masala seasoning when it was done and cooked for another five minutes. I like the spices to be rather strong.

I wasn't a huge fan of the sauce - it seemed to lack body, and I'm not partial to raw onions. I ended up sauteing the mixture for about 15 more minutes (adding some water to further cook the onions and later flour to re-thicken the sauce), upping the spice quantities, and adding a touch of mild to give the sauce more body. (I should also note that I'm living and cooking in Spain, where some conventional ingredients aren't too common. This may have influenced the recipe's success.)

It was a little bland initially (I'm Indian) and I made the following revisions: added 2 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp cumin powder (or you can add extra seeds), an additional tbsp of olive oil, and 2 thai green chillies split down the middle with seeds. It was pretty yummy after that and the flavors do develop with time as someone else noted.

I had to make some changes, I found it bland as written. I used the cumin seeds as stated but ended up adding cumin powder and double the curry powder. I also cooked longer so that the chick peas "absorbed" some of the flavor rather than just be "swimming" in a flavorful sauce. I had to add water (about 1/4 cup) because it was very dry. Will probably make again, with the changes.

Excellent & easy to prepare. I like to use dried garbanzo beans, soak them overnight & boil for 1 hour. The curry powder can make a big difference. I used the House of Spices curry powder which contains coriander, red chilies, cumin, pepper, and fenugreek. Tastes better & is healthier than most restaurants! Thanks for sharing!

Another hit. Used a dry pre-mix of curry spices and canned diced tomatoes. I'm convinced that the curry mix makes it. Also used tapioca flour instead of rice and 1/2 inch of ginger. Not as tomato-y as I'm used too but that'll be fixed next time with addition of tomato paste.

I didn't blend the onions and tomatoes and I used canned diced tomatoes (not the juice just the tomatoes) and I skipped the flour all together. I also added a 1/2 tsp of garam masala and I skipped the cilantro. Easy, simple and quick recipe to prepare.
Easy to make and so delicious that I ate too much. All of these spices are good in chicken recipes, too.

When blending the paste/sauce, I added a clove of garlic. While simmering in the pan, I added some canned coconut milk to it, which also helped to stretch the recipe a bit. Didn't measure just eyeballed it. Overall good dish.

This was ‘pretty good’. I still haven’t found a channa masala recipe that I love. This is just missing a little ‘something’ but I don’t know what that is! Still fresh and tasty but I might try canned tomatoes next time and/or soaking the beans in garam masala or adding it at the end.
Nice Indian curry. Thank you for sharing!
Next time will add firm tofu to make it more hearty.
Thank you, thank you for this recipe! Lovely mild flavor. All three grandkids ate it, even my picky eight-year-old. Into my files it goes!
we added 2 more teaspoons of the curry. Even still I found that it was not a vibrant flavour.

One of my all time favs. Made it for my vegetarian boyfriend and he loved it. I added some garam masala for extra spice. The sauce being an all vegetable purée really adds that fresh taste to this dish. This is definitely one of my go-to recipes.
